title: What does "`Location`-object navigate" navigate?
body:
<https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#location-object-navigate>:

> 1. To **`Location`-object navigate**, given a URL *url* and an optional history handling behavior *historyHandling* (default "`default`"):
>
> 2. Let *browsingContext* be the current global object's browsing context.
>
> [...]
>
> 5. Navigate *browsingContext* to *url*, [...]

<https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects-call-thisargument-argumentslist>

> **10.3.1 \[\[Call\]\] ( *thisArgument*, *argumentsList* )**
>
> [...]
>
> 5. Let *calleeRealm* be *F*.\[\[Realm\]\].
>
> 6. Set the Realm of *calleeContext* to *calleeRealm*.
>
> [...]
>
> 9. Push *calleeContext* onto the execution context stack; *calleeContext* is now the running execution context.
>
> [...]

The above definition seems to suggest that "`Location`-object navigate" should navigate the browsing context of the current operation function's Realm rather than that of `this` `Location` object's relevant global object. This is rather unintuitive (especially when applied on a cross-origin frame) and doesn't match any major browsers' behavior, as confirmed by the following test code:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<iframe src="frame.html"></iframe>
<iframe src="frame.html?setdomain"></iframe>
<script>
    window.onload = () => {
        // current global object's BC = `window[0]`
        window[0].location.href = 'https://www.example.com/';

        // current global object's BC = `window`
        // because of <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#crossorigingetownpropertyhelper-(-o,-p-)>
        window[1].location.href = 'https://www.example.com/';
    };
</script>
</html>
```

`frame.html`:

```html
<script>
if (location.search == "?setdomain") {
  document.domain = document.domain;
}
</script>
```

|                     |                        Result                        |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| WebKit              | Both frames navigate to <https://www.example.com/>   |
| Blink               | Both frames navigate to <https://www.example.com/>   |
| Gecko               | Both frames navigate to <https://www.example.com/>   |
| (Expected per spec) | Top-level BC navigates to <https://www.example.com/> |
